title: fix(integration-tests): TypeScript strict-null errors in test files

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue provides a clear and actionable report of two TypeScript compilation/type-checking errors in integration test files, complete with specific filenames, line numbers, and TypeScript error codes (TS18048 and TS2339).
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: Fixing these type errors requires minor, localized edits in two test files to handle optional fields with null-safe checks (optional chaining) and proper union type narrowing.

summary.problem: TypeScript strict-null and union type errors occur in integration test files hooks-system.test.ts and concurrency-limit.test.ts during type checking.
summary.root_cause: In hooks-system.test.ts, hookCall.stdout and hookCall.stderr are accessed without optional chaining/null checks despite being typed as optional or string | undefined. In concurrency-limit.test.ts, property 'error' is accessed on a toolRequest union type without proper type narrowing.
summary.context: Strict null checking in TypeScript flags potential runtime errors when optional properties or union types are accessed without verifying property existence or handling undefined values.

steps: In integration-tests/hooks-system.test.ts around lines 162-163, add optional chaining or null checks to stdout and stderr accesses (e.g., log.hookCall.stdout?.includes(...) || log.hookCall.stderr?.includes(...)).

In integration-tests/concurrency-limit.test.ts around line 42, ensure toolRequest is properly narrowed or safe property access is used to check for the error property before calling .includes('Rate limit exceeded').

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: TypeScript type check passes without TS18048 or TS2339 compiler errors in integration test files.
verification_steps: Run type checking via npx tsc --noEmit or npm run typecheck to verify all integration test files compile cleanly without strict-null or missing property errors.
